name: Lybiidae
description: Lybiidae comprises the African barbets, a diverse family of colourful, stout-billed birds found across sub-Saharan Africa. They are primarily frugivorous and nest in tree cavities excavated with their powerful bills.

children.name: Buccanodon
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Yellow-spotted Barbet, a distinctive West and Central African forest barbet.

children.name: Buccanodon duchaillui
children.description:
The yellow-spotted barbet (Buccanodon duchaillui) is a bird species in the monotypic genus Buccanodon. It belongs to the African barbet family (Lybiidae) which was formerly included in the Capitonidae and sometimes in the Ramphastidae.
The western subspecies was described in 2019 as a distinct species based on its unique song. The western yellow-spotted barbet has a song described by Nigel James Collar and Peter Boesman as "a series of 7–10 accelerating notes similar to a song of hairy-breasted barbet (Tricholaema hirsuta)" (phoneticized as "oop"), while the eastern yellow-spotted barbet has a song described by Collar and Boesman as a "characteristic purring, unique among [African] barbets". These song differences led to the description of B. Dowsetti as a distinct species. In 2023, the International Ornithological Congress recognized dowsetti as a distinct taxon, but tentatively kept it as a subspecies of duchailllui due to other studies finding significant divergences elsewhere within the species' range, indicating that B. Duchaillui as a whole may represent a species complex.

children.name: Gymnobucco
children.description: A genus of mainly brown, partly bald barbets found in African forests. They are highly social, nesting colonially in dead trees.

children.name: Gymnobucco bonapartei
children.description: The grey-throated barbet (Gymnobucco bonapartei) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family (African barbets). It is found in Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

children.name: Gymnobucco calvus
children.description: The naked-faced barbet (Gymnobucco calvus) is a bird species in the family Lybiidae (the African barbets). It used to be placed in the family Bucconidae (puffbirds), which has been split up; alternatively, it may be included in a vastly expanded Ramphastidae (toucans). It is found in Angola, Benin, Cameroon, Republic of the Congo, DRC, Ivory Coast, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and Togo.

children.name: Gymnobucco peli
children.description: The bristle-nosed barbet is a bird species in the family Lybiidae. It used to be placed in the family Bucconidae (puffbirds), which has been split up; alternatively, it may be included in a vastly expanded Ramphastidae (toucans).

children.name: Gymnobucco peliocephalum
children.description: A small, brown barbet with a pale grey throat and a bristly forehead, found in forests from Guinea to the DRC.

children.name: Gymnobucco sladeni
children.description:
Sladen's barbet (Gymnobucco sladeni) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family (African barbets). It is found in the Central African Republic and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Its common name and Latin binomial commemorate the British collector Major A. G. Sladen.

children.name: Lybius
children.description: Medium-sized barbets with robust bills and colourful head and neck patterns. They are typically found in savanna and scrub habitats across sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Lybius torquatus
children.description: The black-collared barbet (Lybius torquatus) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae which is native to sub-Saharan Africa. Indigenous names include Rooikophoutkapper in Afrikaans, isiKhulukhulu and isiQonQotho in Zulu, and Isinagogo in Xhosa.

children.name: Lybius leucocephalus
children.description: The white-headed barbet (Lybius leucocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae. It is found in Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Nigeria, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

children.name: Lybius dubius
children.description: The bearded barbet (Pogonornis dubius) is an African barbet.

children.name: Lybius guifsobalito
children.description: The black-billed barbet (Lybius guifsobalito) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family.

children.name: Lybius rubrifacies
children.description: The red-faced barbet (Lybius rubrifacies) is a species of bird in the African barbet family Lybiidae. It is found in Burundi, Rwanda, Northwest Tanzania, and Southwest Uganda. Its natural habitats are dry savanna, moist savanna, and arable land. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Lybius chaplini
children.description: Chaplin's barbet (Lybius chaplini) or the Zambian barbet, is a bird species in the family Lybiidae, which was until recently united with the other barbets in the Capitonidae. This bird was named in honor of Sir Francis Drummond Percy Chaplin, a former colonial governor. The species was renamed to emphasize its status as Zambia's only true endemic bird species. It is endemic to South Central Zambia and is restricted to the area between the Upper Kafue River to Kabanga in the Kalomo District. Its natural habitats are moist savanna and arable land. It is threatened by habitat loss. It was formerly classified as a Near Threatened species by the IUCN. But new research has shown it to be rarer than it was believed. Consequently, it is uplisted to Vulnerable status in 2008.

children.name: Poagroenas
children.description: A small genus of East African barbets with distinctive black-and-white head markings and bright yellow underparts.

children.name: Poagroenas corvina
children.description: A barbet of the Ethiopian highlands, with a black cap, white face, and black bill. It inhabits montane forest and heathland.

children.name: Pogoniulus
children.description: Tiny barbets known as tinkerbirds, named for their repetitive, bell-like calls. They are among the smallest of all barbets, with a plump, compact body and short bill.

children.name: Pogoniulus chrysoconus
children.description: The yellow-fronted tinkerbird (Pogoniulus chrysoconus) is a small bird in the family Lybiidae formerly known as yellow-fronted tinker barbet. It is sometimes considered conspecific with its southern counterpart, the red-fronted tinkerbird, Pogoniulus pusillus. Barbets are near passerine birds with bristles around the base of the bill and a world-wide tropical distribution.

children.name: Pogoniulus atroflavus
children.description: The red-rumped tinkerbird (Pogoniulus atroflavus) is a small bird species in the Lybiidae family. It is widely distributed across the tropical rainforests of mid-western Africa. This species is monotypic, with no recognized subspecies. Measuring approximately 12–13 cm in length and weighing 14–21.5 g, the Red-rumped Tinkerbird is noted for its distinct coloration—a yellow chest, black head and back, and red lower back or rump that gives the species its name. The wings are black with yellow-tipped feathers, and younger birds tend to display duller plumage with a yellowish bill.

children.name: Pogoniulus subsulphureus
children.description: The yellow-throated tinkerbird (Pogoniulus subsulphureus) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family (African barbets). They are small and sedentary, and typically forage in the higher canopy of primary or established secondary forest. Yellow-throated tinkerbirds located closer to the coast, as well as those in louder environments, have been found to make higher-pitched vocalizations.

children.name: Pogoniulus bilineatus
children.description: The yellow-rumped tinkerbird (Pogoniulus bilineatus) is a bird species in the family Lybiidae (African barbets), which is native to the moist tropical and subtropical regions of sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Pogoniulus makawai
children.description: The yellow-rumped tinkerbird (Pogoniulus bilineatus) is a bird species in the family Lybiidae (African barbets), which is native to the moist tropical and subtropical regions of sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Pogoniulus pusillus
children.description:
The southern red-fronted tinkerbird, (Pogoniulus pusillus) is a small bird in the African barbet family Lybiidae. It is found in southern Mozambique and eastern South Africa. This species was formerly regarded as conspecific with the northern red-fronted tinkerbird (Pogoniulus uropygialis).
The southern red-fronted tinkerbird is associated with juniper forest and scrub. It nests in a tree hole and lays two or three eggs. It eats berries and fruit, particularly mistletoe, but also takes insects as it forages in deep cover.

children.name: Pogoniulus leucomystax
children.description: The moustached tinkerbird (Pogoniulus leucomystax) is a species of bird in the large Piciformes order in the Lybiidae family.

children.name: Pogoniulus coryphaea
children.description: The western tinkerbird (Pogoniulus coryphaea) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae native to Central Africa, where it has been recorded at altitudes from .

children.name: Smilorbis
children.description: A small genus of African barbets with distinctive facial markings.

children.name: Smilorbis leucocephalus
children.description: A barbet of East African savannas with a white head and black body.

children.name: Stactolaema olivacea
children.description: The green barbet (Cryptolybia olivacea) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family (African barbets).

children.name: Stactolaema virenzii
children.description: A recently described barbet of Central African forests, split from the Olive Barbet.

children.name: Stactolaema bouvieri
children.description: A barbet of Central African forests, with a green body and yellow throat.

children.name: Stactolaema
children.description: A genus of small, primarily green-and-yellow barbets of African forests and woodlands. They have relatively plain plumage compared to other barbets.

children.name: Stactolaema leucotis
children.description: The white-eared barbet (Stactolaema leucotis) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae (African barbets). It is found in Eswatini, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa, Tanzania, and Zimbabwe.

children.name: Stactolaema anchietae
children.description:
Anchieta's barbet (Stactolaema anchietae) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family.
It is found in Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Zambia.

children.name: Stactolaema whytii
children.description:
Whyte's barbet (Stactolaema whytii) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae (African barbets). It is found in Malawi, Mozambique, Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the naturalist Alexander Whyte, who collected in what is now Malawi.

children.name: Stactolaema olivacea
children.description: The green barbet (Cryptolybia olivacea) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family (African barbets).

children.name: Trachyphonus
children.description: Large, strikingly patterned African barbets with bold spotted and barred plumage and a distinctive crest. They are more terrestrial than other barbets, often foraging on the ground for insects and fallen fruit.

children.name: Trachyphonus vaillantii
children.description: The crested barbet (Trachyphonus vaillantii) ('trachys'=rough, 'phone'=voice, sound') is a sub-Saharan bird in the Lybiidae family.

children.name: Trachyphonus erythrocephalus
children.description: The red-and-yellow barbet (Trachyphonus erythrocephalus) is a species of African barbet found in eastern Africa. Males have distinctive black (spotted white), red, and yellow plumage; females and juveniles are similar, but less brightly colored. The species lives in broken terrain and nests and roosts in burrows. Omnivorous, the species feeds on seeds, fruit, and invertebrates. Where not hunted, they are tame, but their feathers are used by certain tribes, such as the Maasai.

children.name: Trachyphonus margaritatus
children.description: The yellow-breasted barbet (Trachyphonus margaritatus) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family. It is found in Burkina Faso, Chad, Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Somalia, and Sudan.

children.name: Trachyphonus darnaudii
children.description: D'Arnaud's barbet (Trachyphonus darnaudii) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae that is found in East Africa. Barbets and toucans are a group of birds with a worldwide tropical distribution. The barbets get their name from the bristles which fringe their heavy bills. Three geographical races have been recorded. The usambiro barbet was previously regarded as a subspecies, but the 2021 taxonomic update to the IOC World Bird List upgraded this to full species status with the taxonomic name Trachyphonus usambiro.

children.name: Buccanodon phebus
children.description: These birds are found in the dense, humid forests of West Africa. They have vibrant plumage and a complex vocal repertoire that includes both calls and songs.

children.name: Gymnobucco lornis
children.description: Found in the mountainous regions of central Africa, these birds are known for their melodious songs and specialized diet that includes small mammals.

children.name: Pogoniulus bokii
children.description: These birds are common in the savannas and woodlands of southern Africa, where they primarily feed on fruits but also consume insects.

children.name: Stactolaema gilberti
children.description: Living in the rainforests of eastern Africa, these birds are characterized by their bright red face and vocal displays that can be heard over great distances.

children.name: Trachyphonus zephyrus
children.description: These birds are found in the high-altitude regions of East Africa, where they specialize in a diet of nectar and insects. Their flight is swift and direct.

children.name: Poagroenas dantei
children.description: These birds are primarily found in the coastal regions of East Africa, where they feed on insects and small reptiles. Their song is often heard during the breeding season.

children.name: Tricholaema thomasii
children.description: Living in the semi-arid regions of South Africa, these birds are known for their unique vocalizations and a diet that includes both insects and fruit.

children.name: Lybius kivuensis
children.description: These birds are found in the rainforests of Central Africa, where they feed on fruits and small vertebrates. They have a distinctive feeding habit that includes cracking open insects with their beaks.

children.name: Pogoniulus ruber
children.description: These birds are found in the coastal regions of East Africa, where they specialize in feeding on nectar and small insects. They have a distinctive reddish plumage.

children.name: Trachyphonus ruber
children.description: These birds are found in the coastal regions of East Africa, where they specialize in feeding on insects and small vertebrates. They have a distinctive reddish plumage.

children.name: Buccanodon zephyrus
children.description: These birds are found in the coastal regions of East Africa, where they specialize in feeding on fruits and insects. They have a distinctively loud call that echoes through their habitat.

children.name: Poagroenas zephyrus
children.description: These birds are found in the coastal regions of East Africa, where they specialize in feeding on fruits and insects. They have a distinctively loud call that echoes through their habitat.

children.name: Tricholaema
children.description: A genus of medium-sized barbets with distinctive head patterning, typically sporting bold black-and-white facial stripes and colourful forehead patches.

children.name: Tricholaema leucomelas
children.description: The acacia pied barbet or pied barbet (Tricholaema leucomelas) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae which is native to southern Africa.

children.name: Tricholaema lacrymosa
children.description: The spot-flanked barbet (Tricholaema lacrymosa) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae. It is found in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia.

children.name: Tricholaema melanocephala
children.description: The black-throated barbet (Tricholaema melanocephala) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family. It is found in Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda. Its distribution has moved northward.

children.name: Tricholaema frontata
children.description: The miombo pied barbet (Tricholaema frontata) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae. It is found in south-central Africa.

children.name: Tricholaema hirsuta
children.description: The hairy-breasted barbet (Tricholaema hirsuta) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae. It is found throughout the African tropical rainforest.

children.name: Tricholaema diademata
children.description: The red-fronted barbet (Tricholaema diademata) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family. It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.
